key_insight: A compact, law-constrained catchment model can match or exceed single LSTM models in streamflow prediction without a daily neural network.
engineering_relevance: Physically structured models offer a competitive alternative to deep learning while retaining explicit water storage and flux relationships.
method: Constrain a storage network using conservation, dissipation and aggregation laws.
Use AI-assisted, literature-grounded refinement to address observed model deficits.
Expand CaRT into CaRT+: 14 states and 35 parameters per catchment.
evidence_signal: Across 602 British, 593 US and 505 Australian catchments, single CaRT+ models achieved median held-out NSEs of 0.863, 0.765 and 0.778; Australian catchments were unused in development.
watch_item: Three-seed LSTM ensembles retained a 0.003–0.012 median paired NSE advantage over the CaRT+ ensemble in Britain and the US.
paper_title: From hydrological laws to catchment models: A process-based model matches deep-learning accuracy on three continents
